payload.headline: QQQ falls further below its 200-day average; SPY nears its 1-month low

summary.thesis: Tech (QQQ) is in a downtrend and slipped further below its 200-day average. The broad market (SPY) still holds its long-term trend but is now 0.9% above its 1-month low. Fear is normal, but only 25% of stocks are above their 50-day average. The selling is wide, not panicked.
summary.decision: Stand aside for both long-term buying and swing trades.
summary.act_at: A QQQ close above 681.41 (its 200-day average) ends the tech downtrend and would support a selective stance. An SPY close below 733.00, then 729.58, would point to a deeper decline.

payload.happening: On Nov 16, SPY closed at 739.95, down 1.91% from 754.37. QQQ closed at 661.75, down 2.67% from 679.89. Over the past 20 trading days, SPY is down 3.46% and QQQ is down 7.88%. Both are below the past year's highest closes, which came on Oct 6: 779.09 for SPY and 759.66 for QQQ. The DATA classes QQQ as a downtrend because it is below both its 50-day (716.59) and 200-day (681.41) averages. It classes SPY as sideways because it is below its 50-day (763.52) but above its 200-day (729.58). The latest stored VIX reading is 19.3 from Nov 13, up from 18.7. The Nov 16 reading isn't stored yet. DATA reports no news since the last note.
payload.business: Taken together, the readings show a broad, orderly pullback led by tech. Trend: tech's long and short trends are both down. The broad market's long trend holds, but its short trend is broken. Fear: the VIX is 19.3, inside the 'normal' 15–20 band, though it ranks at 75 against the past 252 readings. That is near the top of normal, not yet 'elevated'. Weak breadth with only normal fear suggests investors are trimming steadily rather than panicking. That leaves room for more downside before a washout, but it is not a crisis signal either.

worth.text: This is a market note, so no fair value is estimated. The levels below are price-trend markers, not valuations.
worth.key_assumption: No valuation is implied. The levels are price-trend markers only.

bull: SPY is still 1.4% above its 200-day average of 729.58, so the broad market's long-term trend counts as up.
Fear is in the 'normal' band at 19.3, as of Nov 13. The selling has not turned into panic.
Both indices are still above the Nov 5 lows (QQQ 647.05, SPY 733.00), so the recent lows are holding for now.
bear: QQQ is 3.0% below its 200-day average of 681.41 and 8.3% below its 50-day of 716.59. The tech trend is down on both measures.
Breadth fell to 25% of stocks above their 50-day average. Weakness is spread across the market, not just in a few names.
SPY is only 0.9% above its 1-month low of 733.00. A close below it would set a new 1-month low, and its 200-day average of 729.58 sits just under that.

levels.what: QQQ 200-day average. Per the market gate, a close above it ends the tech downtrend. That would support a selective stance.
QQQ 50-day average. A close above it would put tech's short-term trend back up and pass the pipeline's market check. That would be the cue to lean in more.
QQQ 1-month high (Oct 28). A close above it would mean the tech pullback is fully recovered.
SPY 50-day average. A close above it would put SPY's short-term trend back up.
SPY 1-month high (Oct 21). A close above it would mean SPY's pullback is fully recovered.
SPY 1-month low (Nov 5). A close below it would set a new 1-month low, meaning the decline is continuing.
SPY 200-day average. A close below it would put the broad market's long-term trend down too.
QQQ 1-month low (Nov 5). A close below it would mean the tech decline is continuing.

longterm.why: The last note stood aside after QQQ closed below its 200-day average. Since then QQQ has fallen further, from 679.89 to 661.75, and breadth has slipped from 27% to 25%. SPY's long trend and normal fear suggest the damage is contained for now. Still, the readings don't support new buying until QQQ closes back above 681.41.

swing.why: QQQ closed at 661.75, 8.3% below its 50-day average of 716.59. Per the trend gates, setups keep failing the pipeline's market check until QQQ closes above that level.

decision.timing: NVDA reports earnings after the close on Nov 17 (estimated date). Per DATA, it carries big index weight, so its report moves the whole tech group. It lands with QQQ 2.2% above its 1-month low and 3.0% below its 200-day gate. GDP (second estimate, Q3) and October Personal Income and Outlays, which includes the PCE inflation measure, are both due Nov 25 at 08:30. The VIX reading is from Nov 13; the Nov 16 value isn't stored yet.

change_mind: A QQQ close above 681.41, its 200-day average, would end the tech downtrend per the market gate and move the stance toward selective. A close above 716.59 would pass the pipeline's market check.

A SPY close below 733.00 (1-month low), and especially below 729.58 (200-day average), would put the broad market's long-term trend down too and strengthen the case to stay aside. A QQQ close below 647.05 would confirm the tech decline is continuing.
payload.what_changed: Compared with the Nov 13 note: QQQ fell from 679.89 to 661.75 and is now 3.0% below its 200-day average, not just under it. SPY fell from 754.37 to 739.95 and is now 0.9% above its 1-month low of 733.00. Breadth slipped from 27% to 25%. The VIX reading moved to 19.3 (Nov 13), still in the 'normal' band. The moving averages shifted slightly. QQQ's 200-day went from 681.20 to 681.41 and its 50-day from 717.72 to 716.59. SPY's 50-day went from 764.09 to 763.52 and its 200-day from 729.32 to 729.58. DATA reports no news since the last note. The stance is unchanged: stand aside.
